title: Food Storage — Structures, Practices and Storage Environment
shortDescription: Warehouses, silos and cold storage; storage pests; temperature, humidity and gas control.
genZNote: Storage is preservation with a roof. Moisture, temperature, pests — the three boss fights every godown has to beat.

sections.heading: Storage Structures
bullets: Traditional: kothi, bamboo bins, mud bins, earthen pots, Bukhari.
Modern: godowns/warehouses, CAP (cover and plinth) for bulk, steel and concrete silos, hermetic storage, cold storage for perishables, CA (controlled atmosphere) rooms.
Institutions: FCI, Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC), State Warehousing Corporations; WDRA regulates warehouses and negotiable warehouse receipts.
Design needs: dry, rodent- and bird-proof, ventilated, damp-proof floor, dunnage, stack-height limits.

sections.heading: Storage Environment and Interaction
bullets: Safe moisture: roughly ≤ 12% for cereals (lower for oilseeds and pulses) — grain is hygroscopic and equilibrates with air humidity.
Temperature and RH drive respiration, heating and mould; insects multiply at 25–35 °C.

Storage pests: rice weevil, red flour beetle, lesser grain borer, khapra beetle, pulse beetle, Angoumois grain moth, rats; control by hygiene, FIFO/FEFO, fumigation (phosphine), controlled atmosphere, inert dusts.
Cold storage: potatoes ~2–4 °C, apples 0–4 °C, bananas at about 13–14 °C (chilling injury below); ethylene control; CA lowers O2 and raises CO2 to slow respiration.
Interactions: odour absorption, moisture migration, hot spots, mycotoxin build-up, nutrient loss (vitamin C), sprouting/greening in potatoes.

sections.heading: Good Storage Practices
bullets: Segregate by commodity and batch; maintain traceability and stock rotation.
Monitor temperature, humidity, pest activity; use calibrated data loggers.
Hazard control in line with GHP/GMP: cleaning schedules, pest-control logs, no unauthorised chemicals near food.
Cold chain: pre-cooling, reefer transport, consistent temperature to avoid condensation.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Food storage safeguards quality by controlling structure, temperature, humidity, gas composition and pests throughout the storage period.
keyFacts: Phosphine is the common grain fumigant.
CA storage: low O2, high CO2.

highYieldFacts: Methyl bromide is restricted under the Montreal Protocol.
